A growing number of users have recently complained about their Mac displaying a spinning rainbow cursor while running macOS 26.5, with some also reporting that their trackpad becomes completely unresponsive for several seconds at a time.

Activity Monitor typically shows three "culprits," and what appears to be a reliable fix has now been found...

I specifically flagged this issue last month and speculated it might be related to the Apple Intelligence image scanning feature. When checking Activity Monitor, you will typically find one, two, or three processes consuming extremely high CPU usage.

Michael Simon from Macworld has also been affected.

He tried multiple approaches without success, but eventually found one that works: deleting the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. This will, of course, mean that the Mac needs to rebuild the Spotlight index, but he reported the issue did not return after two weeks. My own usage time has been less than a day, but I have not encountered the same problem either.

If you are willing to wait for the Spotlight data to be rebuilt, here is how to delete it:

  • Open a Finder window
  • From the "Go" menu, select "Go to Folder..."
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Press CMD+A to select all, then right-click any item and choose "Move to Trash"
  • Right-click the Trash and choose "Empty Trash"
  • Confirm the action when prompted

If you have been plagued by this issue, please let us know in the comments whether this method works for you as well.
